title: PoisonedEye: Knowledge Poisoning Attack on Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Vision-Language Models
opus_reason: ICML 2025 paper that explicitly extends RAG knowledge poisoning to the multimodal (VLRAG) setting, formalizing retrievability/inducibility properties, proposing three increasingly powerful attack variants, and empirically testing several defenses. Directly relevant to the survey's security_integrity perspective on poisoning and to its broader discussion of attack-defense gaps in retrieval-augmented pipelines.

title: MMed-RAG: Versatile Multimodal RAG System for Medical Vision Language Models
opus_reason: ICLR 2025 paper that directly tackles two canonical robust-RAG failure modes (over-reliance on retrieved evidence and copy-from-context) in the multimodal medical setting. Contributes (a) similarity-gap-based adaptive context selection (evidence construction / action control), (b) RAG-based preference fine-tuning that explicitly addresses cross-modality alignment and ground-truth alignment under noisy/irrelevant retrieval (model evidence use), and (c) empirical quantification of misalignment rates (e.g., 55% copy, 43% over-reliance). Useful as a domain case study illustrating how robust-RAG design principles transfer to medical multimodal LVLMs.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation with Dynamic VQA Dataset and Self-adaptive Planning Agent
opus_reason: Paper directly targets adaptive retrieval planning (OmniSearch) and introduces a benchmark (Dyn-VQA) probing failures of fixed retrieval pipelines under dynamic knowledge needs—both align with the survey's action_control (adaptive retrieval, decomposition, routing) and evaluation perspectives. The diagnosis of 'Non-adaptive' and 'Overloaded' retrieval queries is a clean motivation for adaptive RAG.

title: RAGViz: Diagnose and Visualize Retrieval-Augmented Generation
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: System Demonstrations
opus_reason: RAGViz is an EMNLP demo presenting an open-source diagnostic/visualization toolkit for RAG that highlights token- and document-level attention and supports add/remove document comparison to inspect grounding and hallucination sources. It is not a core method for retrieval noise, defenses, calibration, or benchmarking, but it qualifies as a diagnostic toolkit useful to the evaluation perspective and to model_evidence_use discussions of attribution/grounding.

title: Retrieval Augmented Visual Question Answering with Outside Knowledge
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
opus_reason: This is a multimodal (OK-VQA) RAG paper, not a core text-RAG robustness work. However, it does materially engage with two survey-relevant issues: (i) noisy/misleading retrieval driven by pseudo-relevance labels and how a joint loss can downweight irrelevant documents, and (ii) integrated diagnostic metrics (HSR/FSR/PRRecall) that probe how retrieval and generation interact, which fits the evaluation perspective. Its primary focus is OK-VQA application performance rather than robustness per se, so it best serves as an extended-survey/appendix citation or a multimodal case study, not a backbone citation.

title: VRAG-RL: Empower Vision-Perception-Based RAG for Visually Rich Information Understanding via Iterative Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning
opus_reason: The paper is a vision-specific RAG method that trains VLMs with GRPO to interleave search, visual perception (crop/zoom), and answering, using a composite reward including a retrieval-efficiency (NDCG) term. It is tangential to the core robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence theme but offers a useful boundary example of RL-driven adaptive retrieval and reward-shaping that penalizes noisy retrievals, fitting under action_control with secondary ties to evidence_construction. It is not a robustness/security or faithfulness contribution, so it should not anchor a main robustness section.

title: SearchLVLMs: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Augmenting Large Vision-Language Models by Searching Up-to-Date Internet Knowledge
opus_reason: This is a multimodal (LVLM/VQA) internet-augmented RAG paper. Its hierarchical filtering and diversity selection touch evidence construction (filtering noisy web results, redundancy reduction, context-length-aware selection) and evaluation (a new VQA benchmark for up-to-date knowledge), which are tangentially relevant to robust RAG. However, it is not core to text-based robust RAG under unreliable evidence: no analysis of adversarial/poisoned evidence, knowledge conflict, abstention/calibration, or faithfulness diagnostics. It fits best as an extended/multimodal-application reference rather than a backbone citation.

title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
opus_reason: ColPali is a retrieval method paper introducing a VLM-based late-interaction multimodal retriever and the ViDoRe benchmark. It is positioned within RAG only as a downstream application context. It does not address retrieval noise, distractors, sufficiency selection, knowledge conflict, faithfulness, poisoning/injection, calibration, or abstention. Only the future-work paragraph briefly mentions abstention via Gisserot-Boukhlef et al., which is incidental. The contribution is orthogonal to robust-RAG under unreliable evidence, fitting only as background on modern multimodal retrieval pipelines.

title: Entity-Focused Dense Passage Retrieval for Outside-Knowledge Visual Question Answering
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

It functions as background on retrieval quality issues rather than a venue backbone citation.

title: MuRAG: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generator for Open Question Answering over Images and Text
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
opus_reason: MuRAG is a foundational multimodal RAG architecture paper that extends RAG/REALM/FiD/RETRO to image+text memories using a ViT+T5 backbone with contrastive+generative losses. It does not study any robustness dimension central to the survey: no analysis of retrieval noise/adversarial distractors, no faithfulness/attribution metrics, no knowledge conflict, no poisoning/injection defenses, no calibration/abstention/adaptive retrieval, and no robustness benchmark. The 'distractor setting' is the standard WebQA/MultimodalQA evaluation pool, not an adversarial noise study. The brief discussion of shortcut learning (model gets right answer despite wrong retrieval) is suggestive but anecdotal. It is best cited only as background context on multimodal RAG architectures, if the survey discusses multimodal extension at all.

title: GFM-RAG: Graph Foundation Model for Retrieval Augmented Generation

It is best cited as a representative GraphRAG baseline in extended discussion of evidence construction.

It introduces a truth-grounding metric (scoreh) and evaluates hallucination on WebQSP/CWQ, which weakly support evidence-construction and grounding themes. title: RAGraph: A General Retrieval-Augmented Graph Learning Framework
opus_reason: RAGraph applies the RAG paradigm to GNN tasks (node/edge/graph classification, link prediction) by retrieving similar 'toy graphs' from a key-value vector base and propagating their features/labels into a query graph. Its only contact with the robust-RAG agenda is a brief 'noise-based graph prompt tuning' subsection that cites NLP noise-robust RAG work (Cuconasu, Yoran, Fang) and adds noisy toy graphs during training. The core contribution is graph foundation modeling / graph prompting, not retrieval noise, faithfulness, attribution, poisoning, calibration, or evaluation for LLM-based RAG. It is therefore a boundary example of RAG's cross-modal reach rather than a substantive robust-RAG contribution.

title: RAGGED: Towards Informed Design of Scalable and Stable RAG Systems
opus_reason: ICML 2025 paper introducing RAGGED, a principled evaluation framework with two novel diagnostic metrics (RSS, RSC) that systematically benchmark RAG across retrievers, readers, depths, and datasets while explicitly characterizing reader robustness to noisy/irrelevant context. Directly relevant to the survey's evaluation perspective and also touches evidence construction (noise, distractors, reranking) and action control (depth tuning).

title: Reducing hallucination in structured outputs via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 6: Industry Track)
opus_reason: NAACL Industry Track deployment paper that operationalizes RAG to suppress hallucinated step/table names in JSON workflow generation. It provides concrete enterprise evidence that retrieval grounding reduces fabrication (hallucinated steps from ~16% to <2%; tables from ~20% to <5%) and includes domain-aware retriever fine-tuning with random/BM25/ANCE negatives, plus OOD evaluation. This makes it a credible industry case study for the model_evidence_use and (secondarily) evidence_construction perspectives, but it does not advance core robust-RAG methodology (no adversarial setting, no abstention, no knowledge-conflict handling).

title: LI-RAGE: Late Interaction Retrieval Augmented Generation with Explicit Signals for Open-Domain Table Question Answering

However, the methods are tailored to tables, evaluated only on TableQA benchmarks (NQ-TABLES, E2E-WTQ), and do not study adversarial noise, distractors, calibration, or abstention systematically. It is at best a peripheral example for an extended discussion of explicit reliability signals or joint retriever-reader training, not a core robust-RAG reference.

Its contributions are scalability and benchmark creation for tabular QA, not robust RAG. At best it is a boundary example of structured-data context construction, not a core citation.

title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models

It is most useful as a reference point in an extended evidence-construction discussion (graph-based or structured retrieval alternatives), or as efficiency/cost background, but is not a core robust-RAG citation.

It is useful as supplementary venue-backed evidence for the action_control perspective and partly for evidence_construction (selection/filtering), but does not centrally tackle unreliable-evidence robustness, attacks, calibration, or abstention.

title: FaithEval: Can Your Language Model Stay Faithful to Context, Even If "The Moon is Made of Marshmallows"
Retrieval-Augmented Perception: High-resolution Image Perception Meets Visual RAG
opus_reason: This ICML 2025 paper proposes Retrieval-Augmented Perception (RAP), a visual/multimodal RAG framework using VisRAG to retrieve image crops, a Spatial-Awareness Layout to preserve positional context, and a RE-Search procedure that adaptively chooses K based on model confidence and retrieval scores. It is fundamentally about high-resolution image perception in MLLMs, not robustness of text RAG under unreliable evidence; however, it offers a clear multimodal case study touching on context construction (layout/order) and confidence-driven adaptive retrieval, which are tangentially relevant to evidence_construction and action_control perspectives.

title: Vgent: Graph-based Retrieval-Reasoning-Augmented Generation For Long Video Understanding
opus_reason: This is primarily a domain-specific long-video understanding paper applying GraphRAG plus a structured post-retrieval reasoning step on LVLMs. It touches robust-RAG themes (retrieval noise, hard-negative distractors, post-retrieval filtering/refinement, sufficient context), but the contributions are framed for video QA benchmarks (MLVU, VideoMME, LongVideoBench), not for unreliable-evidence RAG diagnosis in general. It can serve only as a boundary/multimodal example for evidence-construction and context-use perspectives.

title: VimoRAG: Video-based Retrieval-augmented 3D Motion Generation for Motion Language Models
opus_reason: The paper is a domain-specific application of RAG to 3D motion generation, retrieving videos to supplement motion LLMs. It explicitly identifies error propagation from poor retrieval as a problem and proposes McDPO training to teach the LLM when to use vs. ignore retrieved video evidence—conceptually aligned with model_evidence_use and action_control under unreliable evidence. However, the contribution is tightly tied to motion generation (Gemini-MVR retriever, 2D-to-3D motion priors, VQ-VAE motion tokens) rather than generalizable robust-RAG methodology that text-based RAG researchers would adopt.

title: Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
opus_reason: This is a system/application paper introducing EMG-RAG, combining RAG with an editable memory graph and RL-based memory selection for personalized smartphone agents. While it touches adaptive retrieval (relevant to action_control) and acknowledges noise from irrelevant memories, it does not directly address core robust-RAG problems such as retrieval noise robustness, distractors, knowledge conflicts, attribution/faithfulness, poisoning, prompt injection, or calibrated abstention. The dataset, evaluation, and methodology are tailored to a proprietary personalized assistant product, not robust RAG diagnostics.

title: Hierarchical Planning for Complex Tasks with Knowledge Graph-RAG and Symbolic Verification
opus_reason: The paper applies KG-RAG inside a robotic task-planning pipeline (AI2Thor kitchen) with hierarchical decomposition and a PDDL symbolic validator. RAG is one component used to retrieve relevant objects from an ontology; the work neither studies retrieval noise/distractors, faithfulness under conflicting evidence, security, calibration/abstention, nor proposes RAG-specific benchmarks. Its 'verification/correction' loop concerns plan feasibility, not unreliable evidence in the retrieval channel. It is at most a boundary example of neuro-symbolic correction over RAG outputs in a robotics application.

title: Patent Response System Optimised for Faithfulness: Procedural Knowledge Embodiment with Knowledge Graph and Retrieval Augmented Generation
venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Towards Knowledgeable Language Models (KnowLLM 2024)
opus_reason: This is a vertical-domain application paper (patent Office Action responses) combining a domain-trained LLM, a procedural knowledge graph (PPNet), and RAG to reduce six types of unfaithfulness errors. It is not a methodological contribution to general robust RAG—no new retrieval-noise handling, conflict resolution, abstention, or security defense is proposed. Its evaluation is human-only on patent responses with a borrowed/adapted taxonomy from Kim et al. (2024), and the system design is tightly coupled to patent prosecution workflow. At most it serves as a domain case study illustrating how KG-augmented RAG can improve faithfulness in high-stakes professional applications.

title: Multi-Level Information Retrieval Augmented Generation for Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
opus_reason: This is a domain-specific application of RAG to Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering (KB-VQA) on ViQuAE. The contribution is multi-granularity retrieval (entity + passage) with joint training using a CLIP-based entity retriever and DPR passage retriever, evaluated on a multimodal task. While the paper acknowledges that single-step retrieval can yield irrelevant passages and notes the noisy-supervision problem from pseudo-relevance, its central focus is multimodal KB-VQA accuracy, not robustness under unreliable evidence, distractor stress-testing, faithfulness/grounding diagnostics, abstention, or any security threat. It is at most a boundary multimodal RAG reference rather than a core robust-RAG citation.
